title: Instance Segmentation: Align RoIs, Then Paste Masks

questions.question: Why does an instance-segmentation head need more than a semantic class mask?
options: It must produce one mask per object so two objects of the same class remain distinguishable
It replaces every box with one image-wide class ID
It removes the need to localize object boxes
It guarantees a pretrained detector has learned the new classes
questions.explanation: An instance mask is associated with one detected object. A semantic mask labels pixels by class but cannot identify two same-class objects separately.

questions.question: A feature map is 4×4 and represents an 8×8 image. Which spatial_scale maps image coordinates to feature coordinates?
questions.explanation: Feature coordinates are half the image coordinates, so an 8-pixel image span becomes 4 feature pixels and spatial_scale is 4/8 = 0.5.

questions.question: For a `(1,4,4)` ramp and box `[0,0,8,8]` with spatial_scale=0.5, what does 2×2 ROI Align return?
options: A scalar because the box is pooled globally
questions.explanation: The image box maps to feature coordinates 0..4. Bin centers are at (1,1), (1,3), (3,1), and (3,3), which select 5, 7, 13, and 15 from the row-major ramp.

questions.question: Where may `paste_mask` write true pixels for box `[2,3,6,7]`?
options: Only the integer-covered rows 3..6 and columns 2..5
Every pixel in the image with the same class
The whole feature map before resizing
questions.explanation: The mask is resized into the requested box; pixels outside that box remain false. The half-open integer region contains 4×4 = 16 pixels.

questions.question: Why is `mask_bce_with_logits` preferable to applying `log(sigmoid(logits))` directly?
options: It makes every mask positive regardless of the logits
It combines the sigmoid algebraically with log terms and stays finite for large logits
It removes the need for binary targets
It computes IoU without comparing masks
questions.explanation: The stable expression uses max/log1p terms, avoiding overflow or log(0) when logits such as ±1000 are passed.

questions.question: Two 4×4 boolean masks have intersection 6 and union 10. What does `mask_iou` report?
questions.explanation: IoU is intersection divided by union, so the report is 6/10 = 0.6. It is bounded by one for valid masks.
